pitch_detail.notes: Begins in a wide slot at the southwest toe. Go up the right-facing corner, then drift right over slab to a different open corner, passing a smooth stretch with barely enough holds to hold the grade. A step up and left onto another open corner leads to a belay by some dead trees. Easily split into two shorter leads.

Traverse about 15 ft hard left from the belay and enter the corner; 5.9 moves leave the ledge, then it eases, with one short runout midway. Fingerlocks on a slab to the left come near the top, then a 20 ft traverse left along a small ledge to a belay on small cams and a #3. A belay in an alcove below the fingerlocks is an alternative, followed by a direct line through a notch in the roof (not yet climbed).

From the leftward-traverse belay, angle up and right over slab to rejoin the corner crack. Follow the blocky corner into a big roof and pass it either through a small squeeze or on good holds outside it, both 5.9 and the most intimidating moves of the route. Save a #3 for this roof. Belay on a roomy ledge below a flake crack.

Climb the slab just right of the belay, step left at its top and follow a ledge about 10 ft. Then go straight up a blocky, steepening channel that is capped at the top; it protects well. Exit left to avoid loose blocks and belay at a living whitebark tree.

review.changed: Wrote the four pitches the text describes, with grades and lengths as stated. No rappel table: descent is a walk-off down a gully and talus; the text only warns that bailing by rappel would cost lots of gear.
review.other_findings: Stored pitches=5 but the text climbs it in 4 long (55-65 m) pitches; pitch 1 can be split in two. Stored length 219 m matches the four pitches summed.

pitch_detail.notes: Easy start in the far-left right-facing corner, mostly 4th class, in a band of red argillite. The gully collects loose rock, so step onto the left wall to dodge the choss and watch for rockfall onto the belayer. A few 5th class moves reach the belay ledge; build the anchor as far left as possible to reduce rope drag on the next pitch.

The better pitch. Traverse hard left to a slab under a right-facing corner that runs into a roof. Get right under the roof, then shift left and round the arete, staying off the loose flake in the roof for hands or gear. The face above, on slabs and cracks, ends at a little grassy ledge. The belay is inside a corner that faces left; scramble the last ledges to the walk-off. Rope drag is likely; a few double-length slings help.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches with stated grades and lengths. No rappel table; descent is a walk-off.

pitch_detail.notes: Start on the west side atop the stacked grassy ledges, below the biggest triangular roof, at a shallow left-facing corner. Go through it, up a short right-facing corner, then follow cracks to a detached block with a finger crack. Belay in the corner right of the block.

Go directly up blocky ground to a trough of easier angle and cross it rightward to a left-facing corner beneath a small roof. Get gear high in that corner, take an airy step and slab up to the ledge under the stacked roofs, keeping small cams for the anchor. The ledge is loose, so move carefully above a follower.

Move left beneath the roofs and up the steep left-facing corner, the hardest moves of the route, on small footholds. Good holds at the top of the corner get you out, and a dirt slope above leads to a tree belay.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches with stated grades and lengths. No rappel table; descent is a scramble and walk-off, and rappelling would mean leaving a lot of gear.

pitch_detail.notes: From the start platform follow intermittent cracks up the middle of the slab. One fixed angle sits in a crack. Seepage is possible in spring or after storms. Protection is spaced, with runouts around 30 ft. Belay in a left-facing corner in blockier ground.

Angle up and left off the belay until you can enter the right-facing dihedral that sweeps in from the left, then follow its curve rightward over looser steps to a tree belay. Bring at least three double-length slings to extend placements in the dihedral.
Head left off the belay or right into the left-facing dihedral; this pitch is looser, so protect the belayer from falling rock. Go straight up between stacked choss to solid trees.

review.changed: Wrote the three pitches with stated grades and lengths. No rappels; descent is a walk off.

pitch_detail.notes: Stand the belayer uphill and right of the crack, out of the way of falling choss. Climb easy, loose ground to the crack start, then up the crack past good but runout gear to a small roof, pulled on good but possibly loose jugs. Above, the crack fades; continue to a big ledge at the foot of a stemming corner. Stem as much as possible and test holds. Belay in a diagonal crack, saving a 0.5 for the anchor.

Cross the ledge into the corner system and climb to the huge roof with white blocks beneath; do not pull on those blocks. Work alongside the roof crack on face and slab moves and pull onto a ledge, which is the crux. Above is easy 5.4 slab with little protection, steepening and improving near the ledge. A diagonal crack there takes a 0.75 for the anchor.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches; 110 ft converted to 34 m. No rappel table: descent is a hike and crawl through a hole.

pitch_detail.notes: Opening pitch of the right-hand flow on the upper headwall.
Treated as one linked stretch of sustained WI4 ice.
Steepest pitch of the flow, rated WI4+.
Final pitch eases to WI3. A left bypass of pitches 4 and 5 combined goes at WI3+ over about 80 m.

review.changed: Wrote pitches 1, 2-3 (given as one linked 85 m section), 4 and 5 with stated grades and lengths. Notes are short because only grades and lengths are stated. No rappel table.
review.other_findings: Stored length 457 m looks off; the pitches given sum to about 225 m.

pitch_detail.notes: Bolted sport pitch with a bolted anchor at the top.
Bolted sport pitch, the hardest on the route, ending at a bolted anchor. Watch for a chert feature along the way.
Short final pitch on bolts to a bolted anchor. Adjacent pitches can be linked with about 20 draws.

review.changed: Wrote three pitches with stated grades and lengths. No rappel table: only 'rappel the route, knot the ends' and a 70 m rope are stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Easy rock that gradually steepens, trending slightly right beside big chert features, and finishing on a sloped ledge where the belay is on bolts.

A technical section leads up and right off the belay to a bigger slanting ledge that has bolts for an anchor; stopping there is possible. Climbing on up the headwall is better, with the crux near the top and another set of bolts for the belay, making a long lead.

review.changed: Wrote two pitches with stated grades. No lengths stated. No rappel table: only 'three rappels' is stated (a 70 m rope falls short of the bush ledge, reaching a smaller ledge about 8 ft above it, needing easy downclimbing).

pitch_detail.notes: Climb the ice pillar that sometimes reaches the ground, or start on the sheet above if the pillar has not formed. The pillar can look sound but may hide a wide crack beneath its lip with air behind it. Above the lip the sheet is mellow, calf-burning WI3. Belay on a small natural ledge near the top, or in a small ice cave on the left.
Roughly half a rope length of easy WI3 with three topping-out choices. The left one is typically steepest and has a good rappel tree just beyond the lip.

review.changed: Wrote two pitches; no per-pitch grade for pitch 1 is given and no lengths. No rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Begins where the third pitch of Blaster ends. Take the main gully straight up over rolling ice for about 50 m, to a snow ledge.
Steeper, with several vertical steps. Pick a line and go a full 65 m to the rock above or to a tree on the far right.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches; no grades per pitch. No rappel table: descent is rappel back to the snow slope, walk skier's right, then rap Blaster on trees and v-threads, not a definite numbered list.

pitch_detail.notes: Start up the fat flow high in the central gully, coming out of the left side, and diagonal right above the gully.
Choose one of three pillars and climb it to the top. Difficulty ranges from WI4 to WI5 depending on the pillar.

review.changed: Wrote two pitches with stated grades. No lengths. No rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Several short vertical ice steps up to a snow slope.

Swing right around the rock buttress and enter the mixed corner system, which you follow over snow, ice or mixed terrain for most of a rope length. The best stance is in the corner shortly before the route moves right.
Traverse out to the right and finish up the last steep wall on the best ice available. From the top, either walk the snow slope about 100 ft to the last ice step or rappel the route.

review.changed: Wrote three pitches with stated grades. No lengths. No rappel table: rappelling the route is only mentioned in passing.

pitch_detail.notes: Mantle-heavy, blocky climbing with some loose rock and runouts. Easy moves reach a high first bolt; then work right to the second, up a broken corner of blocks where small-cam gear is marginal. Keep following bolts through twisting moves, mantles and more questionable gear to the anchor.

The best pitch. Easy ground leads to a ledge, which you follow left to the foot of the crack. Protection is very good throughout; place the 0.75 in the pod only after you have climbed past it. Pull over a steep lip and continue up slab to the anchor.

Short. Left on crimps to below a flake and bulge, then a big move up to the flake is the crux. Follow the weakness to a small ledge, placing small cams and wires, to the anchor. A 5.10 variation: from the ledge go right 10 ft, make spooky moves into a crack, and jam to easier ground.

review.changed: Wrote three pitches with stated grades. No lengths or bolt counts given. Added the pitch 3 variation in notes. No rappel table: only 'retreat with one 70 m rope' is stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb a curtain of ice about 5 m wide to a steep snow ramp that leads up and right.
An easier slab of ice up to the trees, where the anchor is.

review.changed: Wrote two pitches; no per-pitch grades or lengths given.

pitch_detail.notes: Steep start that eases after about 15 m. Set up a screw anchor ahead of the next steep bit and belay there.
Treated as combinable: a series of steep steps leads to the trees. There are several ways to top out, and going left is easier.

review.changed: Wrote pitch 1 and a linked 2-3; no grades or lengths. The stored count is 3 but pitches 2 and 3 are described together.

pitch_detail.notes: Start up a steep curtain, then a low-angle ramp to a free-hanging curtain, which only rarely reaches the ground. Belay on bolts to the left of the curtain.
The mixed pitch: reasonable rock, well protected dry-tooling. Belay on bolts below the last stretch of ice.
The last 120 ft up the obvious ice gully, which can be a scratchy chimney and stemming affair or a steep, narrow runnel depending on the season. Belay at big spruce trees at the top.

review.changed: Wrote three pitches with the described belays; no grades. Pitch 3 length is converted from 120 ft. First-ascent history left out.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb a ramp to a couple of ice daggers, the crux, which protects very well. Clip a bolt, then climb ice and rock to a ledge with a tree anchor.
Several options up and left, in the middle, or on the right, all good.

review.changed: Wrote two pitches; no per-pitch grades or lengths.

pitch_detail.notes: Thin ice up to a ledge.
A ramp trending left leads to the top, where a tree serves as the anchor.

review.changed: Wrote two pitches; no grades or lengths.

pitch_detail.notes: Steep from the start on well-featured good ice. After about 30 m it eases to WI3 and then WI2. Belay off a tree.
Cross a short snowfield, then go roughly straight up about 200 ft on WI2-3 ice.

review.changed: Wrote two pitches; pitch 1 length is the steep section only, stated about 30 m, pitch 2 converted from 200 ft.
